text: The development of carpentry is not solely reliant on tools, but also on materials and techniques that facilitate construction and ensure durability. Varnish, a common protective layer for wooden structures, provides a barrier against water damage and maintains the appearance of the wood. In contrast, joints are integral to a structure's structural integrity and performance. High-quality joints prevent cracks and splits, ensuring the structure's longevity and stability. Moreover, joints can be designed with cleaning, maintenance, and repurposing in mind, making them a valuable asset to any carpentry project. The ultimate aim is to produce a stable, functional, and aesthetically pleasing structure that withstands the test of time.
